title: GraspSearchResponse
description: grasp-search service -> BFF output. Top-N ranking with score breakdown. Wire form uses camelCase.

candidates.description: Ranked candidates, rank ascending (1 = best). Not a single best pose.

diagnostics.description: Solver-decided facts about the search as a whole (the rejection funnel), so a client can explain an empty or thin result. Contract v4 (ADR-081) widens the funnel to the three validation domains -- visible (Vision) / reachable (Path: reach, IK, interference) / graspable (Grasp). Invariant: candidatesGenerated = rejectedByReach + rejectedByVisibility + rejectedByIk + rejectedByInterference + rejectedByGrasp + feasible (stages are exclusive; the filter short-circuits in the engine's measured cheapest-first order: reach -> IK -> grasp -> visibility -> interference, which decides which single stage a multiply-infeasible candidate is attributed to). Requests that declare no camera / no gripper always report 0 for the corresponding rejection stage. Presentation (wording, colors, meters, ladder-risk mapping, suggestions) is derived client-side and never carried here. Contract v8 (ADR-157) splits rejectedByInterference by motion phase (interferencePhases) and can carry an all-phase analysis (interferenceAnalysis). Contract v10 (ADR-158 PR1) adds the arm measured along the approach / lift paths to the all-phase analysis (interferenceAnalysis.armPath) -- measured, never counted as a rejection. Contract v11 (ADR-158 replay stage) adds, per returned candidate, the samples the judgement used (interferenceAnalysis.replays) -- progress within a phase, never seconds or a frame rate.

rejectedByVisibility.description: Rejected because the declared camera cannot see the grasp point (occluded sightline or outside the field of view). Always 0 when the request declares no camera.

rejectedByGrasp.description: Rejected by the geometric grasp gate of the declared gripper (opening width / finger clearance / contact-pair existence). Always 0 when the request declares no gripper.

feasible.description: Candidates that passed all five checks (= scored).

returned.description: Candidates actually included in candidates[] (= min(feasible among the set the strategy returns, topN)). Without grasp specs, or under `score` order, that set is every feasible candidate; under `priority` it is only the first spec with a feasible candidate (ADR-152 D5).

reachNearestMiss.description: Smallest distance by which a reach-rejected candidate missed the reachable shell (same length unit as the request geometry). null when nothing was rejected by reach.

occlusionNearestMiss.description: Smallest occlusion depth among visibility-rejected candidates (how deep the most-blocking obstacle cuts the closest-to-visible sightline; same length unit as the request geometry). null when no visibility rejection has a measurable occlusion depth (e.g. only outside-FOV rejections, or none at all).

graspNearestMiss.description: How close the best grasp-rejected candidate came, as a CLOSED KIND-DISCRIMINATED union (ADR-118, contract v5). Replaces v4 `openingNearestMiss`, whose name and unit assumed a parallel jaw: a suction cup misses by a seal-patch shortfall, not by an opening width, and reporting one as the other would have the client draw a meter labelled in the wrong quantity. null when no grasp rejection has a measurable miss (e.g. only contact-pair-missing rejections, or none at all), and always null when the request declares no gripper. `kind` is the discriminator and each branch is closed -- field presence is implied by kind, never optional. STRUCTURE (DEF-029, 2026-09-15): the `null` case sits OUTSIDE the discriminated union rather than as a third branch beside the two kinds. Semantically identical -- exactly the same instances validate -- but `null` was never a `kind`, and expressing it as one made the schema uncompilable under ajv strict (`discriminator` requires `type: object`, which a nullable union cannot declare). That is why this package's own test lane could not run.

graspSpecs.description: Per declared grasp spec, in request order, how many candidates it generated and how many passed every stage (ADR-152 D4, contract v7). EVERY sent spec has a row, including the ones whose candidates the strategy did not return -- a spec that was not returned and a spec that had nothing are different facts (原則 #31). Empty when the request sent no spec. Per-stage rejections per spec are not carried (deferred).

interferencePhases.description: Interference broken down by MOTION PHASE (ADR-157 D2/D3, contract v8), EXACTLY one row per phase in motion order: transit, approach, close, lift, transport, place. A phase is `evaluated` or `unevaluated` purely from the request's declarations (never per candidate). An evaluated row's `rejected` counts the candidates whose FIRST colliding phase it was (a candidate is attributed to the earliest phase it hits -- closing is only asked of a hand that got in). Invariant: the sum of `rejected` over evaluated rows = rejectedByInterference. An unevaluated row carries a closed `reason` and NO `rejected` -- 0 and not-judged are the same number otherwise (ADR-120). `notYetDecided` marks phases the solver has no method for yet (transit/transport/place); the rest name the missing declaration.

interferenceAnalysis.description: The all-phase interference analysis (ADR-157 D6, contract v8), a CLOSED KIND-DISCRIMINATED union. `firstCollision` = not requested (the default; stated as a branch, never by omitting the key). `allPhases` = requested via graspSearch.interferenceAnalysis: every evaluated phase was judged to the end for every candidate that reached the interference stage, and the hits are counted per phase / part / obstacle. The answer itself (candidates, ranks, the funnel) is identical in both modes.

graspSpecId.description: Which declared grasp spec (request `target.graspSpecs[].id`) produced this candidate, or null when it came from the derived `surfaceSamples` (ADR-152 D4, contract v7). REQUIRED and nullable rather than optional: a closed layer grows no optional siblings (ADR-060), and 'no spec' is a stated fact, not an omitted one. A client does not reverse-engineer the spec from the pose -- under `score` order 'not in the top N' and 'had no candidate' would be indistinguishable.

pose.description: The pose the solver *decided*, as a closed kind-discriminated union. Only solver-decided facts ride the wire; presentation (approach vector, ghost color, gripper-width display, animation) is derived client-side from the frame + convention and is NOT part of this contract. The only intentional growth point is adding a new kind (which bumps contractVersion). kind is the discriminator; each branch is closed (additionalProperties:false). 'optional' is not a design word here -- field presence is implied by kind.

poseEndEffector.description: End-effector (hand/tool) pose expressed in a base/world frame. Cartesian.

poseJointSpace.description: Pose expressed in the joint space of a named kinematic chain.

chainRef.description: Which kinematic chain (robot) the joint values belong to.

cartesianFrame.description: A rigid-body pose in a base/world frame.

scoreBreakdown.description: Per-candidate score breakdown explaining why a pose ranked where it did. Contract v4 (ADR-081): the five booleans mirror the domain-staged filter (visible = Vision domain, withinReach/ikSolvable/interferenceFree = Path domain, graspable = Grasp domain). A returned candidate passed every stage, so all five are true; `visible` / `graspable` are vacuously true when the request declared no camera / no gripper (the request itself carries which case applies). Contract v6 (ADR-135) adds `reachSolution`: the joint configuration the solver decided, so a client can DRAW the reaching arm instead of only reading a boolean. `ikSolvable` stays -- the skeleton is an additional way to confirm reach, not a replacement for the flag.

objectiveScores.description: objective name -> normalized 0-1 value (absolute basis, so scores are comparable across requests).

totalScore.description: Weighted sum of the normalized objective scores.

openingMiss.description: Parallel jaw: the smallest amount by which the jaws failed to span the object.

shortfall.description: Required width minus the jaw max opening (same length unit as the request geometry).

sealPatchMiss.description: Suction cup: the smallest amount by which the sealable flat patch fell short of the cup.

shortfall.description: Cup diameter minus the diameter of the flat-enough patch found at the contact point (same length unit as the request geometry).

reachSolution.description: The JOINT CONFIGURATION the solver decided for this candidate, as a CLOSED KIND-DISCRIMINATED union (contract v6, ADR-135). A returned candidate always passed the IK stage (the filter short-circuits, so an IK-rejected candidate is never in candidates[]) -- what this union discriminates is therefore NOT reachable/unreachable, which `ikSolvable` already carries, but whether a DRAWABLE joint vector exists at all. It exists only when the request declared `robot.kinematics` and the closed-form solver ran; with no declaration the wrist-cone proxy judges reachability without producing joint angles, and there is nothing to draw. Required on every candidate: the absence of a joint configuration is DECLARED, never signalled by omitting the field (原則 #31). Presentation (how the arm is animated into the pose, ghost color, whether a preview is shown at all) is derived client-side and is NOT part of this contract (ADR-060).

reachSolutionSolved.description: A representative joint configuration that reaches this candidate's pose. One solution, not all of them: the closed form admits up to 8, and stage 0 asks only whether the pose is reachable, so the solver picks one deterministically (ADR-127 D5).

joints.description: Joint angles in RADIANS, in the chain order of the declared `robot.kinematics` (base to flange). Exactly six -- the closed form is derived for that exact structure, so a different count is a different arm.

reachSolutionUndeclared.description: No joint configuration was determined for this candidate. The fact is the absence itself, not any one cause of it: typically the request declared no `robot.kinematics`, so reachability was judged by the wrist-cone proxy (ADR-127 D3) which produces no joint angles, but any producer that judges reach without solving joints reports this branch. The client MUST NOT draw an arm pose for this candidate -- inventing one would show a configuration no solver decided, which is exactly what ADR-135's goal forbids.

graspMiss.description: The measured miss of the best grasp-rejected candidate, as a CLOSED KIND-DISCRIMINATED union (ADR-118). `kind` is the discriminator and each branch is closed -- field presence is implied by kind, never optional.

interferencePhase.description: One motion phase's interference row (ADR-157 D2). `kind` is the discriminator; each branch is closed.

rejected.description: Candidates whose first colliding phase this was.

candidatesAnalysed.description: Candidates that reached the interference stage (the population every evaluated phase was judged on).

phases.description: Evaluated phases only, in motion order (unevaluated ones are explained by interferencePhases).

collided.description: Candidates that hit something in this phase. NOT exclusive across phases.

hits.description: Per (part, obstacle), how many candidates hit it in this phase; most first.

part.description: tcpPath = the TCP's path (stands in for an undeclared hand shape); held = the grasped object carried from lift on.

obstacleIndex.description: Index into the request's obstacles[]. Naming it is the sender's job -- names never ride the wire.

replays.description: Per returned candidate, in rank order and exactly one per returned candidate: the samples the judgement used, phase by phase (ADR-158 replay stage, contract v11). Only evaluated phases appear, in motion order (unevaluated ones are explained by interferencePhases). Time is progress within a phase (s in [0,1]) -- never seconds, never a frame rate: the frames between samples are derived by the client and are judged by nobody.

armPath.description: The arm measured at the pick pose and along each phase's straight TCP path (ADR-158 PR1, contract v10). A MEASUREMENT, not a judgement: the search still judges the arm at the pick pose only (approach x arm = atEndOnly), so a candidate whose arm touches something only on the path stays among the returned candidates. Population = candidatesAnalysed. Each path point solves IK again and takes the solution nearest the previous point's, starting from the representative solution judged at the pick pose -- the same branch is followed, never searched for one that misses. A CLOSED KIND-DISCRIMINATED union: `undeclared` = robot.kinematics is not declared, nobody decided the arm's joints, nothing was measured (not 'no hits').

pathSamples.description: Points per phase path, both ends included (s = i/(pathSamples-1), progress within the phase -- not seconds).

atPickPose.description: Candidates whose arm touches something at the pick pose -- the same pose the search judges in the approach phase.

hits.description: Per obstacle the arm (links + tool segment) touched, how many candidates; most first.

phases.description: Evaluated phases with a decided straight path (approach always, lift when declared), in motion order. The pick-pose point is excluded from these rows.

onPath.description: Candidates whose arm touches something at some path point other than the pick pose (may also touch at the pick pose).

onPathOnly.description: Of onPath, those whose arm is clear at the pick pose -- hits the current judgement does not see.

noSolutionOnPath.description: Candidates with some path point that has no joint solution within limits (the arm cannot follow the straight line there).

hits.description: Per obstacle the arm (links + tool segment) touched, how many candidates; most first.

replayHit.description: A part the judgement checked at this sample, and the obstacle it touched. The arm is never here -- whether the arm was judged or only measured is the arm's own kind.

part.description: tcpPath is a segment test: a sample's tcpPath hit belongs to the stretch from the previous sample to this one.

replayArm.description: The arm at one sample, as a CLOSED KIND-DISCRIMINATED union. judged = the pose the search judged (the approach phase's pick pose); measured = a pose only measured along the path (ADR-158 PR1 -- never counted as a rejection); noSolution = measured, but no joint solution within limits at this point; undeclared = robot.kinematics is not declared, nobody decided the arm's joints (draw no arm).

oneOf.title: replayArmUndeclared
oneOf.description: No kinematics declared -- the arm was not placed.

oneOf.title: replayArmNoSolution
oneOf.description: No joint solution within limits at this point.

oneOf.title: replayArmJudged
oneOf.description: The arm pose the search judged.

obstacles.description: Indices into the request's obstacles[] the arm (links + tool segment) touches at this sample.

oneOf.title: replayArmMeasured
oneOf.description: An arm pose only measured (not used to reject).

obstacles.description: Indices into the request's obstacles[] the arm (links + tool segment) touches at this sample.

rank.description: The returned candidate this replay belongs to.

replayPhase.description: One evaluated phase. A phase with a straight TCP path (approach, lift) carries its samples; closing the hand is judged as ONE swept volume with no instants inside it, so it carries that volume's hits only -- no samples are invented.

samples.description: In motion order, both ends included.

s.description: Progress within the phase (0 = phase start, 1 = end). Not seconds.

tcp.description: TCP position at this sample (on the phase's straight line; the orientation is the candidate's and does not change).

hits.description: Empty = judged here and touched nothing.
